audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only two months of NDS despite valuing the post-acquisition company
audit_findings.magnitude: NDS contributed $48.8 million of FY2026 sales and a $4.7 million continuing-operations net loss; filed pro forma FY2026 sales and ADS net income were $239.316 million and $29.537 million higher, respectively; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The $455.9 million OE anchor reflects only February 2 through March 31 of NDS operations, while forecast growth is applied to that anchor as though it represented the entire post-acquisition perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 2, 2026, we completed the acquisition of National Diversified Sales (“NDS”).
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation identifies the acquisition and partial year, contrary to the audit's statement that no perimeter event was reported, but identification does not cure the anchor mismatch. NDS represented 23% of consolidated assets at acquisition and generated $94.7 million of sales in the following full quarter. The filed pro forma figures demonstrate that the missing period is large enough to affect normalized earnings and potentially the valuation conclusion. The exact OE increase cannot be established from sales or GAAP net income alone.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-acquisition trailing-twelve-month OE using the same OE rules, reconcile it to NDS pro forma results and acquisition financing, and rerun all scenarios without crediting unfiled synergies.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset additions may escape the maintenance-capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.687 million of FY2026 finance-lease asset additions, equal to 9.4% of the $455.9 million OE anchor; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease depreciation is added back in OE but the corresponding noncash asset additions are excluded from maintenance investment, OE is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has operating and finance leases for plants, yards, corporate offices, tractors, trailers and other equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $42.687 million of finance-lease additions and $40.602 million of principal payments. It does not establish how much represented maintenance rather than growth or whether the OE workpaper already included an equivalent replacement charge. The potential exposure is nevertheless material relative to the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 depreciation add-backs, cash capex, finance-lease additions and lease principal by asset class; identify the maintenance portion and rerun OE once, avoiding any double deduction of financing principal.

audit_findings.title: KSOP redeemable common shares require an explicit denominator reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: Worst-case 4.533 million-share omission would increase the denominator from 77.157359 million to 81.690359 million, reducing base value from $85.12 to approximately $80.40, bull value from $94.81 to approximately $89.55, and buy-below from $59.58 to approximately $56.28
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted KSOP share increases the fully diluted denominator and reduces value per share without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s KSOP holds shares of redeemable common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The balance sheet separately reported 4.422 million redeemable shares at June 30, while the July 30 cover count of 75.405342 million appears consistent with including KSOP shares after intervening repurchases, but an explicit roll-forward is absent. Even assuming the larger March 31 balance of 4.533 million was entirely omitted, the resulting value remains far below the $135.76 market price and only strengthens the existing valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document a share roll-forward from June 30 common shares plus KSOP redeemable shares through the July 30 cover date, then reconcile restricted stock, options, performance units and ESPP dilution; rerun only if the reconciliation reveals an error larger or different in direction from the tested 4.533 million-share case.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains a large restructuring charge of uncertain recurrence
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.299 million FY2026 pre-tax expense, including $31.234 million of noncash charges and $15.864 million paid; a further $5.336 million was recorded in the June 2026 quarter; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained episodic cash restructuring costs depress anchor OE, while removing recurring realignment, integration or replacement costs would overstate normalized OE and growth economics.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the 2026 Restructuring Plan, for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recorded expense of $ 48.3 million related to the optimization of the Company’s production, recycling and distribution networks, including the closure of four facilities and changes to the Company’s production footprint.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross FY2026 charge equals 10.6% of the OE anchor before tax and OE classification effects. Much of it was noncash accelerated depreciation or impairment that may already be neutralized by OE add-backs, but cash costs continued into the next quarter and the company could not estimate the plan's remaining cost or end date. Both permanent retention and complete exclusion could materially misstate value.
audit_findings.action: Trace every restructuring component through net income, depreciation and other OE adjustments; separate noncash write-downs, completed closure cash costs, recurring operating costs and forecast integration costs, then rerun normalized OE with documented treatment.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition transaction costs may be permanently embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.3 million of FY2026 NDS transaction costs, equal to 8.8% of the $455.9 million OE anchor before tax and OE adjustments; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing-specific costs retained in anchor OE suppress every forecast year, while excluding an economically recurring acquisition program cost would inflate normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Company incurred $ 40.3 million of transaction costs related to the acquisition such as legal, accounting, valuation and other professional services.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed amount is large enough to affect the valuation if retained, but the supplied record does not show its exact after-tax contribution to OE or establish an appropriate recurring acquisition-cost allowance. The following quarter also included $3.2 million of transaction and integration costs, showing that related spending had not ended.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $40.3 million through the OE calculation, separate transaction costs from integration and recurring corporate-development costs, establish a historical recurring acquisition-cost allowance, and rerun all scenarios using that normalized amount.

audit_findings.title: Adding all cash assumes none is required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure of $162.251 million, or approximately $2.10 per diluted share; removing all cash would reduce base value from $85.12 to about $83.02, bull value from $94.81 to about $92.71, and buy-below from $59.58 to about $58.11
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating or restricted cash should be excluded from the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our operations are working capital intensive, and our inventories, accounts receivable and accounts payable are significant components of our net asset base.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, especially given working-capital intensity and $110 million of open capital orders. However, even the deliberately conservative assumption that none of the $162.251 million is excess cash reduces value by only $2.10 per share and leaves the market price well above the bull value, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile unrestricted domestic cash, foreign cash, restricted cash, seasonal liquidity needs and committed expenditures; adjust the bridge for identified required cash, but no conclusion-changing rerun is needed unless additional bridge liabilities are found.
